title: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Indices (July 2026 data) — 9:00 a.m. ET, the 1-step print that sets the October edition's base
source: EST: two primaries read direct on 2026-09-09 by this lane, one of them different from the proposing lane's. (1) press.spglobal.com's June-2026-data release (2026-08-25-S-P-Cotality-Case-Shiller-Index-Reports-Annual-Gain-in-June-2026, HTTP 200, 90,693 bytes) states the publisher's own rule verbatim: "The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Indices are published on the last Tuesday of each month at 9:00 am ET." September 2026's Tuesdays are the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th, so the last is 2026-09-29, and the release's own two-month lag (published 2026-08-25 reporting June 2026) puts July 2026 data on it. (2) FRED's series page for CSUSHPINSA (fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CSUSHPINSA, HTTP 200) states "Next Release Date: Sep 29, 2026" against "Jun 2026: 336.663, Updated: Aug 27, 2026" — a live scheduled date for this exact series, and a STRONGER second primary than the release calendar the proposing lane cited, because it is series-specific rather than a listing. The proposing lane's second source could NOT be reproduced from this runner: fred.stlouisfed.org/releases/calendar?rid=199 returns HTTP 200 but renders its date table client-side, so the payload this runner received contains no release dates at all (recorded in the ledger's probe-ref.blocked as NO_DATA_RENDERED, never silently substituted). Filed `estimate` on taxonomy, not date doubt: CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs has no member for an index provider's own publication rule, and FED: is scoped to the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar rather than to a Reserve Bank's series metadata. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by the never-assessed initial research on this id, after reading the single proposal that carried it (proposals/case-shiller-hpi-2026-09-29.from-case-shiller-hpi-2026-10-27.json, now shadowed). Ledger: docs/research/events/case-shiller-hpi-2026-09-29.md. THE PROPOSAL'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS CONFIRMED AND ITS SECONDARY CLAIM IS REFUTED. Confirmed: this is the 1-step print, and it is the tightest edition this series ever offers — June is the last published month, so the persistence forecast for July carries a 0.1186pp MAE and a 90% band of [-0.180%, +0.333%] on the national SA m/m, against the 0.201pp / [-0.30%, +0.57%] the October edition sits at today (FRED CSUSHPISA, 2015+, n=137, reproduced independently of the proposing lane). Refuted: the proposal called 09-29 "the cleaner slot of the two" because it is not an FOMC day. Measured on the proposal's own metric it is the DIRTIER slot — 41 tracked events sit within five days of 2026-09-29 against 24 around 2026-10-27, including quarter-end on 09-30 with the Russell style recapping and the Select Sector secondary reweight effective that morning, PCE and GDP Q2 third on 09-30, ISM on 10-01 and the September jobs report on 10-02. Not-FOMC is not clean. NEW THIS SESSION, and it revises how the sibling ledger's Detroit item should be read: the Wayne County outage is a ROLLING ONE-MONTH LAG THAT BACKFILLS, not an accumulating hole. The publisher states the mechanism verbatim in the same release that announces the gap ("There was, however, enough data to calculate a valid May 2026 update... S&P DJI will continue to provide updates to the Detroit index values for the month(s) with missing sale transactions data"), and the live FRED vintage measures it: DEXRNSA ends 2026-05 while CSUSHPINSA and all five peer cities checked end 2026-06, and January 2026 — the month the March-2026 release said would have no valid update — is present today at 195.422.
